_comment: Signs of a threat (Expansion 6): scenes played when you walk into a village its threat has begun to trouble. They need nothing from the player. Words: {villain} the threat's name, {home} its lair, {place} the village.

threat_mourning.about: The villagers carry one of the dead in from the fields on a hurdle; a crowd gathers, a mourner kneels and keens, and the bearers take the dead away to be buried.

murmur: Who is it? Who have they brought in?
Cover the face, for pity's sake.
That is the third since the new moon.
Found him past the last fence. What was left of him.
Keep the children indoors.
{villain} again. It can only be.
God keep him. He was a quiet man.
Nobody goes out after dusk now.
keen: Oh, my love. Oh, my own love, what did it do to you?
He went to see to the sheep. Only to see to the sheep.
I could not even wash him. There was not enough to wash.
Who will tell the little ones? Who will tell them?
Every night I hear it. Every night, and now it has him.
Get up. Please get up. It is only the cold.
The sheep came home without him. They knew.
bearer: Gently now. We have a long walk and a short grave.
The priest is waiting. Let us through.
Keep your eyes off, those that cannot bear it.
Another for the churchyard. We shall run out of ground.
Mind the hurdle. It is all we had to carry him on.
No one is to speak of how he was found.

threat_wake.about: The priest comes out into the square to bless the doors against the dead; a crowd gathers, a villager says their buried father was seen walking, and the priest says the words.

murmur: Chalk the lintels. Chalk them all.
They say the barrow is open.
I heard the churchyard gate last night. Nobody opened it.
Bar the doors and keep the dogs in.
Salt on the sill. It is all my mother ever said to do.
It was the cold, I told her. It was only the cold.
{villain} has called them up. Mark my words.
Hush. Let the priest speak.
seen: My father, Father. In his shroud. Walking by the well.
I buried him myself, and there he was at the end of our lane.
He did not look at me. His feet were bare and black with earth.
He stood at the door all night and never knocked.
I saw his face in the moon. It was not the face I buried.
He is dead ten winters. Why would he come back now?
words: Peace, child. What walks is not your father. Only the shape of him.
The dead are not theirs to call. They are God's, and shall be given back.
Do not speak to them. Do not open to them. Whatever they say.
Go home, bar the door, and say the evening prayers aloud.
I have prayed over {place} since midnight. I do not know that it was enough.
I will lay hands on every door. That much I can do.
bless: May no cold hand lift this latch. May no dead foot cross this stone.
Light before, light behind, and the door between shut fast.
Let the grave keep its own, and the night keep to itself.
Rest the dead. Spare the living. Amen.
From the wanderer in the dark, deliver us.
Go in peace. Go in, and go in early.

threat_robbed.about: A carter staggers in at the gate, stripped and beaten by robbers on the road; he shouts what was done in the square, a crowd murmurs, and a guard says there is nothing to be done.

cry: Robbed! They took the lot - cart, horse, coat and all!
Is there no law here? Is there nobody?
Four miles out! They were waiting in the trees!
They took everything but my life, and that was close!
Look at me! Look what they did!
{villain}'s men! I saw the badge on the cloak!
murmur: The road is not safe any more.
That is the fourth this month.
Where's his horse? Where's his cart?
Somebody fetch him a blanket.
{villain}, I'll be bound.
My cousin was due in by that road.
Nobody dares carry goods past {home} now.
They'll be at our doors next.
told: There were nine. Masked. One of them laughed the whole while.
They said the toll was paid to {villain} now, and took double.
I knew the road. I have driven it twenty years. They knew me too.
They left me in the ditch with a warning. Pay the toll, or walk.
A man with a lord's voice said I was lucky. Lucky!
They were gone before I could stand. Into the hills, towards {home}.
answer: We have six men, a ditch and a rusted gate. What would you have us do?
Go after nine, in their own woods? I have a wife.
Write to the lord. Much good it will do. Aye, write.
I am sorry. Truly. There is nothing the watch can do.
Sit down, friend. Have something warm. That is all I can give.
If anyone is fool enough to try, it will not be the watch.

threat_refugees.about: People fleeing the country round the threat's lair come in at the gate one after another and make for the square; one falls and is helped up, a crowd gathers, and they say what they fled.

murmur: More of them. Where are they coming from?
Look at their feet. They have walked for days.
They have brought nothing. Not a bundle between them.
Is there food for them? There is hardly food for us.
They came from up by {home}, I heard.
Give the poor soul some air.
If they are running, what are we staying for?
Fetch water. Quickly.
help: Up, friend. Up now. Lean on me.
Just a little further. There's the well.
Someone give us a hand here, please!
Don't stop now. We are nearly safe.
You're all right. You're here. Get up.
fled: We left at night. We left the fire still burning.
Everything we had is behind us, near {home}.
The cattle were taken first. Then the neighbours.
My roof is burnt. My field is salted with blood.
We heard it in the hills for weeks. Then it was in the yard.
We saw {villain}'s work. We did not stop to look twice.
fled_more: The whole valley is on the road. We are only the first.
There's nothing left past the river. Do not go that way.
Is there a priest? Is there anyone who will take us in?
Hold fast to your doors. It will come this way too.
We have not eaten in two days. Do not ask us more yet.
If you have any sense, you'll pack your things and come with us.
